ai.description: This slender, worm-like snake reaches 20 cm. It is uniform dark brown to black with a blunt, rounded head and tail. Key features include a distinct rostral scale and a subocular gland.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Argyrophis bothriorhynchus* is best distinguished by its preocular scale, which is vertically divided or notched, a unique feature absent in most other Indian blind snakes.
ai.habitat: Günther’s Blind Snake inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found in leaf litter or loose soil at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: Günther’s blind snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil in search of ant and termite larvae.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Argyrophis bothriorhynchus* is oviparous, laying small clutches of elongated eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Argyrophis bothriorhynchus is found in the Eastern Himalayas and Northeast India, primarily occurring in West Bengal and Assam at low to moderate elevations.
